column1: # Obligation citations — goal 0009 (select which recorded context crosses a harness boundary).
# One row per rule of this increment that a gate-runnable Go test discharges, in the four id spaces the
# increment's rules come from:
#   D1–D5   the goal's five `Done when` clauses, in order (docs/goals/0009-selective-context.md).
#           D5's arms are split so each refusal shape has its own row and its own test (an ill-formed
#           specification; the grammar half answered without a read; the usage exit code and "nothing was
#           written" asserted through the CLI), and D3's two arms (the counterpart carried, the strict
#           refusal) are two rows as well, because the goal proves them "in both directions";
#   B1–B2   the goal's two `Bounds` clauses, in order;
#   S1–S4   the rules of AGENTS.md's selection paragraph ("A conversion carries only what the caller
#           selected …"), in the paragraph's own order — the opt-in flag with the untouched default path
#           and the read's own ordinal space; the recorded-link seam (a call and its result carried
#           together, the counterpart named with the ordinal that pulled it in); the refusals (the core's
#           own sentence, the usage exit code, nothing installed) and the strict arm; the report's four
#           classes with the transformation named in both surfaces.
#   S5      the read-line sentence the fix stage added to that paragraph: the line the target's loader
#           walks is the read's own, and a selection neither moves a record onto it nor off it.
# scripts/obligation-citations.py is the arbiter: every row's cited test must exist in the named package
# and run and pass, and the `citations` step is required — a tree that lost this file, or a citation that
# went stale, fails the gate instead of passing partially. Columns: rule_id, test, package, artifact.
# Tab-separated; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored; a rule id appears once.
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate evidence is a throw-away probe, a native harness
# run, or a python case the required `selftest` step runs cannot hold one):
#   D4 — "a run without a selection flag is byte-identical to the same run before the change". Its evidence
#          is the throw-away before/after probe docs/evidence/0009-selective-context.md §4 quotes: one test
#          file converting documents through the five routes and through the pipeline itself, the flag
#          absent in every run, run on HEAD's tree and on this one, with the two runs' printed lines and
#          normalized written bytes diffed. A probe that must exist only between two revisions is not a
#          gate step's subject, which is the same form-based carve-out 0007 and 0008's manifests state.
#   D1's native half — "the target is natively loadable": the evidence is the recorded run's
#          `verification.load: verified` (Codex's own app server, `thread/resume`, quoted with its version
#          in the record's §1). A native harness run is deliberately not a gate step.
